- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and model is underestimating, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2), model often fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward 10–15-day moving average within 3–5 days.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence or sentiment stabilizes.
